Specify a floating catchment area index without data

Source: R/08-spax_fca_spec.R
spec_e2sfca.Rd

Experimental. spec_2sfca(), spec_e2sfca(), spec_m2sfca(), spec_3sfca() and spec_huff2sfca() declare a floating catchment area (FCA) index with its decay and its options, as the data-free counterparts of spax_2sfca(), spax_e2sfca(), spax_m2sfca(), spax_3sfca() and spax_huff2sfca(). A specification holds no data and no fitted value: an FCA index is computed, not fitted, so every decay needs its sigma (or its threshold) here.

Usage

spec_2sfca(threshold)

spec_e2sfca(
  decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 30),
  normalize = c("identity", "standard", "semi")
)

spec_m2sfca(
  decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 30),
  normalize = c("identity", "standard", "semi")
)

spec_3sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 30), selection = NULL)

spec_huff2sfca(
  decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 30),
  selection = NULL,
  attractiveness = "supply",
  alpha = 1
)

# S3 method for class 'spax_fca_spec'
format(x, ...)

Arguments

threshold

For spec_2sfca(): a single finite number greater than 0, the largest travel time in the catchment, or a named numeric vector of such numbers, one per demand group.

decay

The decay of the weights: a decay with a value for sigma (decay_gaussian(), decay_exponential(), decay_power(), decay_custom()), decay_step() or decay_inverse(); or a named list of these by demand group.

normalize

The normalization of demand: "identity" (the default), "standard" or "semi".

selection

The decay of the selection weights, in the form of decay; NULL (the default) uses decay.

attractiveness

"supply" (the default), or a numeric vector named by facility with finite values of 0 or more.

alpha

A single finite number of 0 or more: the exponent of the attractiveness in the selection probability.

x

An FCA specification.

...

Unused.

Value

A spax_fca_spec (also a spax_spec): a list with kind ("2sfca", "e2sfca", "m2sfca", "3sfca" or "huff2sfca"), decay, normalize, selection, attractiveness, alpha and threshold. A field that the method does not have is NULL.

Details

Decays. A decay is decay_gaussian(), decay_exponential() or decay_power() with a number for sigma, or with a SpatRaster of sigma values (a variable catchment); decay_step() or decay_inverse(); or decay_custom() with a kernel declared by decay_kernel() and a number for sigma. "fit" is refused, and so is a bare kernel name, which means sigma = "fit". With demand groups, decay and selection can be a named list by group, and threshold a named numeric vector by group.

  • spec_2sfca(): the original two-step method with a binary catchment of travel time threshold, with no demand normalization.

  • spec_e2sfca() and spec_m2sfca(): the enhanced and the modified methods with distance decay decay. normalize is the normalization of demand: "identity", "standard" or "semi" (see calc_normalize()).

  • spec_3sfca(): the three-step method. selection is the decay the selection weights are built from; NULL (the default) means the same decay as decay.

  • spec_huff2sfca(): the Huff-model selection. attractiveness is "supply" (the supply measure) or a numeric vector named by facility with one finite value of 0 or more per facility, and alpha is its exponent.

See also

decay_step(), decay_gaussian(), decay_kernel()

Other access interface: decay_step()

Examples

spec_2sfca(threshold = 15)
#> <spax spec> 2SFCA
#>   decay  step (threshold): 15
spec_e2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 10))
#> <spax spec> E2SFCA
#>   decay      gaussian (sigma = travel scale): 10
#>   normalize  identity
spec_m2sfca(decay = decay_exponential(sigma = 0.2), normalize = "standard")
#> <spax spec> M2SFCA
#>   decay      exponential (sigma = rate): 0.2
#>   normalize  standard

# Selection with another decay than the weights
spec_3sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(10), selection = decay_inverse())
#> <spax spec> 3SFCA
#>   decay      gaussian (sigma = travel scale): 10
#>   selection  inverse: 1/(d + 1)

# Huff selection with an attractiveness named by facility
spec_huff2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(10),
               attractiveness = c(a = 2, b = 1), alpha = 2)
#> <spax spec> Huff-2SFCA
#>   decay           gaussian (sigma = travel scale): 10
#>   selection       same as decay
#>   attractiveness  2 values ^ alpha 2

# Demand groups: a decay for each group
spec_e2sfca(decay = list(young = decay_gaussian(8), old = decay_step(20)))
#> <spax spec> E2SFCA
#>   decay      by group: young gaussian (8), old step (20)
#>   normalize  identity
